title: sdk(auth): align env var names + precedence with Python/Go (deprecate legacy names)
author: Dana Lo
description: Summary: Aligns TS SDK authentication environment variables and resolution precedence with the Python and Go SDKs as part of the SDK parity initiative. This change also introduces deprecation warnings for legacy env var names to reduce "works in TS but not in Python" issues and to standardize support/debugging instructions. Motivation: Support + SE feedback shows customers frequently set different env vars per language and are surprised by which value wins when both are present. We’re standardizing on a single set of env var names and a single precedence order across SDKs, with security-reviewed guidance to avoid leaking secrets in logs/errors. New behavior (matches Python/Go): Precedence order: (1) explicit client option (apiKey / bearerToken) (2) environment variables (standard names) (3) none -> throw a typed auth error. Standard env vars supported: REDWOOD_API_KEY for API key auth; REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN for bearer token auth; REDWOOD_BASE_URL remains as-is for endpoint override. Legacy env vars (still accepted, now deprecated with a warning): RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, REDWOOD_TOKEN. If multiple env vars are set: explicit client option always wins; between env vars we prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY over deprecated key vars; bearer token is only used when api key is not present (same as other SDKs). Deprecation warnings: Warnings are emitted once per process (guarded) and do not print secret values. We include guidance text pointing to the migration notes and the new standard names. Error handling: Missing credentials now throws RedwoodAuthError with message safe for logs; error includes "source" metadata (explicit/env/none) but never includes the credential string. Tests: Adds unit coverage for precedence, deprecation warning behavior, and non-leakage. Also updates the README auth snippet to reference REDWOOD_API_KEY / REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN consistently. Notes: This PR intentionally does not change header formats beyond existing behavior (Authorization: Bearer ...). This also keeps backwards compat: legacy env vars will continue to work for at least 2 minor versions; removal will be tracked separately after customers have had time to migrate. Related: ENG-5122 (env var alignment), INT-1182 (better error metadata / support triage).
commits: sdk(auth): introduce AuthResolver and normalize credential sources
sdk(auth): support REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN with parity precedence
sdk(auth): accept legacy env vars w/ one-time deprecation warnings
tests(auth): add coverage for precedence + warning emission + redaction
docs(readme): update auth examples to standard env vars
changed_files: High-level changes: packages/sdk/src/auth/resolveAuth.ts (new centralized resolver with explicit/env precedence); packages/sdk/src/client.ts (wire auth resolver into client construction and error surface); packages/sdk/src/errors.ts (add RedwoodAuthError w/ safe messaging + source metadata); packages/sdk/src/constants/env.ts (standard + legacy env var names and warning text); packages/sdk/test/auth/resolveAuth.test.ts (new tests); README.md (auth snippet + env var names). Small illustrative snippet (resolve order): `if (opts.apiKey || opts.bearerToken) return { kind: 'explicit', ... }; const apiKey = env('REDWOOD_API_KEY') ?? envLegacy('RW_API_KEY'); const bearer = env('REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN') ?? envLegacy('REDWOOD_TOKEN'); if (apiKey) return { kind: 'env', scheme: 'api_key' }; if (bearer) return { kind: 'env', scheme: 'bearer' }; throw new RedwoodAuthError('Missing Redwood credentials. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN, or pass apiKey/bearerToken explicitly.');`
ci_checks: CI summary (GitHub Actions): lint (pass), typecheck (pass), unit tests (pass), build (pass), bundle-size (pass). Initial run failed once due to a flaky "bundle-size" upload step; rerun succeeded with no code changes.
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (requested changes): "Can we ensure the precedence matches the draft standard exactly? Specifically explicit param > env var, and within env vars prefer standard names over legacy. Also please make the deprecation warning one-time; we don't want spam in server logs." Dana Lo (author): "Updated resolver to prefer standard vars and added a `warnOnce()` guard keyed by env var name. Added tests for both." Marcus Lin (security): "Please confirm we never log the actual secret or include it in thrown errors, even in debug mode. Also avoid printing the full env var value in deprecation warnings." Dana Lo: "Confirmed; warnings reference only the env var name. Added regression test asserting error messages do not contain any provided credential string." Sabrina James (Python/examples): "Can you align naming with Python: REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN (not ACCESS_TOKEN)?" Dana Lo: "Yes, updated to REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN and marked older TS-only aliases deprecated." Mateusz Zielinski (Go): "In Go we treat bearer token as fallback if API key is present. This matches your current approach—thanks. One nit: can we include a short note in the warning pointing to migration notes?" Dana Lo: "Added link text to docs path and kept it generic for published docs." Final approvals: Ibrahim Khan (approved), Marcus Lin (approved after security nit), Sabrina James (approved), Mateusz Zielinski (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash to main by Dana Lo. Squash commit message: "sdk(auth): align env vars + precedence; deprecate legacy names". No rollout flags; behavior is backwards compatible due to legacy env var support + warnings.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK: Auth env vars are now standardized with Python/Go. Use REDWOOD_API_KEY or REDWOOD_BEARER_TOKEN. Legacy env vars (RW_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_TOKEN, REDWOOD_TOKEN) still work but will emit a one-time deprecation warning and may be removed in a future minor release.
